title: Acknowledge spoofed-source budget-exhaustion ceiling for broadcast accounting in security analysis
description: Security-pass finding from project-LICHEN-worker6-0adq (pre-existing gap, not introduced by the relay-key fix). The §6.3.3 broadcast relay budget key (now the full primary /128) is not authenticated end-to-end for broadcast traffic: link-layer Schnorr signatures are per-hop (relays re-sign with their own keys, 02-physical-link.md:305-308), OSCORE is pairwise/unicast, DAO-origin auth is DAO-only. A radio adversary can mint fresh keypairs for fresh budget identities (Sybil) or spoof sources to exhaust victim budgets; 06-security.md's DoS treatment (:18 generic row, :1319 jamming only) does not acknowledge this ceiling. The §6.3.3 note now states the ceiling inline; add matching treatment to 06-security.md's threat/DoS analysis (coordinate with nqz6.3.3's audit scope) describing the residual risk and why per-hop budgets remain worthwhile despite it.
close_reason: DONE (worker2). Added the acknowledged ceiling to spec/06-security.md §8.1 (after the DoS threat row): the 04-network.md §6.3.3 broadcast relay budget keys on the packet's source IID field, which the limiter never binds to an authenticated identity — per-hop LLSec re-signs (02-physical-link.md:305-308), OSCORE (pairwise or group) secures CoAP payloads not the network-layer source, DAO-origin auth is DAO-only (§8.4). E2E-signed broadcast classes exist (SOS origin sigs, announces) but the limiter does not consult them. Fresh budget identities are FREE (arbitrary source IIDs under one existing keypair; IID spoofing also pressures the un-capped relay-state table); budgets remain worthwhile as amplification limiters, not proof of origin. Ceiling acknowledged, not closed (§8.4 scopes E2E origin auth to DAO). Coordinates with the open 06-security addressing-consistency audit (nqz6.3.3 scope, named descriptively not by ephemeral ID). NOTE: this tree's §6.3.3 still keys on IID — the 0adq '/128 relay-key' fix and its inline ceiling note landed on another branch; the acknowledgement is written to be true for the current IID key and stays true after the /128 migration (both are unauthenticated source fields). 3x codereview delegated to kimi-k3: 5 findings, all fixed — (1) IID-vs-/128 key-shape inversion vs this tree (rewritten to match current §6.3.3 IID key); (2) 'OSCORE is pairwise/unicast' false (group OSCORE exists — rephrased to payloads-vs-source-field); (3) 'no E2E broadcast signature exists' overbroad (SOS + announces counterexamples — narrowed to 'the limiter does not consult them'); (4) 'mint identities at key-generation cost' overstates evasion cost (IID spoofing is free — corrected); (5) §8.7->§8.4 citation + ephemeral bead ID removed from spec prose.
